episode_profile.title: From Molecules to Memories: The AI Approach to Scent Detection
episode_profile.topic_summary: In this episode, Alex Wiltschko discusses the intersection of neuroscience and technology in scent detection. He explains how AI is being used to predict and create new fragrance molecules, the complexities of olfactory perception, and the potential applications of this technology in various industries.

key_arguments.claim: AI can predict the smell of molecules better than human perfumers.
key_arguments.speaker: Alex Wiltschko
key_arguments.context: Wiltschko discusses the advancements in AI that allow for accurate predictions of scents based on molecular structure.

key_arguments.claim: The olfactory sense is more complex than previously understood, with 350 distinct channels of information.
key_arguments.speaker: Alex Wiltschko
key_arguments.context: Wiltschko explains the intricacies of the olfactory system and its implications for AI scent detection.

key_arguments.claim: Osmo's AI platform can discover new fragrance molecules that are safe and effective.
key_arguments.speaker: Alex Wiltschko
key_arguments.context: Wiltschko highlights the company's focus on creating new scents that meet safety and performance standards.

key_arguments.claim: The future of scent technology includes the ability to capture and replay smells digitally.
key_arguments.speaker: Alex Wiltschko
key_arguments.context: Wiltschko envisions a future where smells can be digitized and stored, similar to how images are handled.

key_arguments.claim: AI can help design insect repellents by understanding the olfactory preferences of both humans and insects.
key_arguments.speaker: Alex Wiltschko
key_arguments.context: Wiltschko discusses a collaboration with the Gates Foundation to create effective mosquito repellents using AI.
